mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in WORKPLACES mobility shifts time from commuting to local discretionary shopping, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks. The signal is strongest when RESIDENTIAL stays elevated, because more time at home increases neighborhood retail trips.
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES remains below its recent mean but RETAIL_REC does not rise relative to the prior four weeks over the next 28 days, this mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT turns upward while WORKPLACES stay soft, access to shopping corridors improves without a matching rise in office-driven trips, pushing RETAIL_REC higher within two weeks. The effect should fade if transit gains are not maintained.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above its t-3w level and remains positive for 2 consecutive weeks
failure_condition: If TRANSIT stays positive for two straight weeks but RETAIL_REC does not improve over the next 14 days, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A continued increase in GROCERY_PHARM indicates consolidated essential trips and more local errand chaining, which spills into nearby retail visits and raises RETAIL_REC over the following week. This is an always-on short-lag signal.
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM rises week-on-week but RETAIL_REC does not increase within the next 7 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An upswing in PARKS mobility signals favorable weather and outdoor activity that competes with indoor retail, reducing RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks. The effect should appear only when PARKS is above its recent baseline for multiple weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS stays above the t-3w level for 2 consecutive weeks
failure_condition: If PARKS remains elevated for two weeks but RETAIL_REC is not lower than in the prior four weeks over the next 28 days, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A drop in TRANSIT combined with a drop in WORKPLACES is a tightening-mobility regime that suppresses discretionary shopping flows and lowers RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks. The mechanism fails when only one of the two series falls.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both fall below their prior-week means
failure_condition: If both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES drop below their prior-week means but RETAIL_REC does not decline within 14 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Elevated RESIDENTIAL mobility reflects more time spent near home, which supports neighborhood shopping and modestly lifts RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks. The effect is stronger when GROCERY_PHARM also stays elevated.
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL remains above baseline but RETAIL_REC does not outperform its last-four-week mean over the next 28 days, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in TRANSIT is a short-lag access shock that feeds into retail visits within one week, but only if WORKPLACES are not simultaneously falling. If work mobility weakens at the same time, the retail lift is canceled.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT increases by at least 3 points week-on-week
failure_condition: If TRANSIT rises by at least 3 points week-on-week and WORKPLACES are flat or rising, but RETAIL_REC does not increase within 7 days, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in PARKS and rise in GROCERY_PHARM indicates a shift from outdoor leisure toward local errand-based trips, which raises RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks. This pattern should be strongest in the late-week shopping regime.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls while GROCERY_PHARM rises for 2 consecutive weeks
failure_condition: If PARKS declines and GROCERY_PHARM rises for two straight weeks but RETAIL_REC does not increase relative to the prior four weeks over the next 28 days, the hypothesis is rejected.
